text:
maria: Hey team — quick Q on private deploy hardening. We're planning a 'rootless' onprem image for customers (FIPS enabled + KMS via customer HSM). Two asks: what minimal RBAC changes do we need for the runtime to access the customer's KMS shim, and any gotchas for NetworkPolicies / conntrack when we deny-by-default?

devin: For RBAC — prefer scoped service identities instead of cluster-admin. Create a ServiceAccount per-tenant runtime, grant only kms:Encrypt/kms:Decrypt (or equivalent) via an external role mapping. Avoid writing broad secrets in cluster. :thumbsup:

ash: Also add iam:Sign or HSM-specific ops if the runtime needs attestation keys. In many customers the KMS shim calls back to a local agent on 127.0.0.1: we needed hostNetwork or a specific netpol exception.

maria: Good point re local agent. We want network isolation but still let the runtime talk to host-agent. How to express that in netpol without opening too much?

sre-jordan: Use namespace-scoped NetworkPolicy with an allow rule to the podSelector for the host-agent DaemonSet IPs via a dedicated namespace or label, e.g., label agents:kms-proxy. Then default deny for everything else. Avoid hostNetwork if possible; if agent runs hostNetwork, add a short, well-scoped egress rule to the node IP range.

devin: Watch conntrack: heavy short-lived flows between runtime and agents can exhaust conntrack on kernels with small tables, especially if customers enable NAT gateway. For rootless containers conntrack entries may stick. Recommend connection pooling or unix domain sockets for local shim.

ash: Unix socket is best. If not possible, add a liveness/readiness check that reuses a single long lived connection. Also document sysctl settings we ask customers to bump (net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max).

maria: About audit logging — customer will insist we ship audit events to their SIEM. We currently log KMS requests (masked) in runtime audit. Any compliance concerns with logging plaintext resource IDs?

sre-jordan: Mask sensitive fields. In FIPS environments, ensure hashes are computed with approved algorithms (SHA-2 family) and keys are never logged. Send structured JSON events with event.type, principal, resource, outcome. Avoid logging ciphertext or raw plaintext keys.

sec-bot: Automated note: CI policy requires a passing risk-review for changes to kms client code. Link: https://redwood.internal/policies/kms-client-change :eyes:

devin: On incident side, if KMS failures happen (HSM offline), runtime should fail closed for secrets access but still serve non-sensitive cached items. Have a fallback policy: return 503 for new decrypts, and an explicit metric (kms.decrypt.failures) to trigger pagers.

ash: For vuln triage: we found an upstream libsec v2.1.3 CVE that affects our envelope implementation. Quick plan: patch to v2.1.4 (no API change), add a short-lived feature flag to fallback to software-signing if HSM has issues, and schedule an emergency rollout in Dedicated/Private images.

maria: Can someone drop a minimal RBAC + NetworkPolicy example snippet we can include in the onboarding doc?

sre-jordan: Sure — minimal examples below (paste into docs). Use least privilege, label the agent NS 'kms-agent'.

```
# ServiceAccount binding (kubernetes RBAC)
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: runtime-kms-role
  namespace: customer-runtime
rules:
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["secrets"]
  verbs: ["get"]
- verbs: ["use"]
  resources: ["services"]
# bind to SA
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: runtime-kms-binding
  namespace: customer-runtime
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: runtime-sa
  namespace: customer-runtime
roleRef:
  kind: Role
  name: runtime-kms-role
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
```

```
# NetworkPolicy: allow to kms-agent only
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-to-kms-agent
  namespace: customer-runtime
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: runtime
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          role: kms-agent-namespace
      podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: kms-proxy
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 1812
```

maria: This is great — thanks. Two follow-ups: 1) Do we need to recommend sysctl changes in onboarding for conntrack? 2) Where to record HSM operator runbook for fallback?

devin: 1) Yes, suggest min nf_conntrack_max 131072 for high-throughput tenants and provide a monitoring dashboard. 2) Put HSM runbook in private repo under ops/runbooks/hsm-fallback.md and reference from onboarding. Include playbook steps: fail closed, alert infra, escalate to customer HSM ops, rotate ephemeral keys if integrity suspect.

ash: I'll open a small PR for the RBAC + netpol examples and add a short troubleshooting section on conntrack + UDS recommendation.

maria: Perfect. If anyone has test clusters to validate conntrack behaviour under rootless containers, ping me — happy to help run load profiles. :raised_hands:
